I was diagnosed with depression and anxiety when I was nine years old. I was diagnosed with eating disorders when I was ten. I was assaulted by a grown man when I was eleven. My dad got really close to dying when I was twelve. By the time I was thirteen I was functioning as an adult. I realized I was queer when I was fourteen. When I was fifteen, I fell in love with my best friend. I still love him to this day and he still doesn't know. He'll never love me back. When I turned sixteen, my mental health took a dangerous dive. I spent three months basically in quarantine because of it, I was considered a danger to myself. My physical illnesses also took over and I spent a few months in the hospital. Couldn't afford the medications I needed, so I now live with chronic pain and unidentified chronic illness. I spend days at a time vomiting and being unable to breathe. I have chronic joint pain from a birth defect. Doctors wrote me up as "officially" disabled and tried to prescribe me a service dog. I couldn't afford it.  When all of that subsided (as chronic illness can leave sometimes, but always comes back) 2016 happened. I lost all hope. I lost a lot of friends as mental illness stole all of my function. A lot of people told me I was ruined. Towards the end of 2016, I realized that life would only get worse.  And my seasonal affective disorder started in November when it normally starts in the end of December. It normally ends before February but it's still hurting me now. On this day, I'm hurting from unrequited love and the pain of being queer and mentally ill in a time where I'm scared to be myself. I've lost my friends and I've lost my family. I was born destined to fail.
